subject: 6193A5AE5579E4039E4D0589AE21DACA
introduction: “I am a child of tender years. Nourish me from the breast of Thy mercy, train me in the bosom of Thy love, educate me in the school of Thy guidance.” The guide begins with prayers put into a child’s own mouth, continues with prayers of parents for the unborn, the newborn and the growing child, widens to all “the children that are born in Thy day” and to schools, and ends with prayers for youth and for one’s descendants. Hannah, who “lent” her son to the Lord, and the mother of Mary in the Qur’an, whose vow reading 11 repeats, prayed the dedication; Zachariah and Abraham prayed for offspring; the Psalms see sons “as plants grown up in their youth” and children as “an heritage of the Lord”. The Gospel scenes of blessing and the growth of the child Jesus stand beside the infants’ prayers. Wordsworth’s child “trailing clouds of glory”, Blake’s question whether the maker of the lamb made the tiger, and Gibran’s “your children are not your children” ask what a child is and whose.
questions: What does it do for a child to have a prayer in their own voice (“I am a child”)? Which phrases would a young child understand and keep?
Reading 11, Hannah and the mother of Mary each dedicate a child before birth. What is being promised, and by whom can such a promise be kept?
The prayers return constantly to gardens, saplings and flowers. What does that imagery assume about how children grow and what adults owe them?
Wordsworth thought the child brings a glory that fades; the prayers ask that the child be educated. Do these pull in different directions?
Reading 28 prays for schools. How do prayer for children and practical provision for them belong together?

outside.why: “I am a child of tender years. Nourish me from the breast of Thy mercy.” The Psalmist looks back to the same beginning: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother’s breasts; thou art my God from my mother’s belly.
I have behaved and quieted myself, as a child that is weaned of his mother: my soul is even as a weaned child.
“Make of me a shining lamp and a brilliant star.” Ye are the light of the world. Let your light so shine before men.
An innocent child asking to be guarded and trained. The child Samuel, called in the night, is taught what to answer: speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.
“I am a child; enable me to grow.” And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
A fresh sapling in the garden. That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace.
Children who have drunk the milk of divine knowledge. Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength.
Destitute children, yet the verdure beside Thy stream. He shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom.
Be a shelter for this poor child. A father of the fatherless is God in his holy habitation.

“I am a young child, a suppliant, a captive. Be Thou my refuge.” Whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me; but whoso shall offend one of these little ones, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck.

“I dedicate that which is in my womb to Thee.” The prayer is that of Mary’s mother in the Qur’an: my Lord! I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated offering. Accept it from me.
Hannah: for this child I prayed; therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.
Gibran says to parents what such a dedication admits: your children are not your children; they come through you but not from you. What does a parent give up in praying reading 11?
Let this infant be fed from the breast of Thy mercy. And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.
Guard this babe in the cradle of safety. And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
Make the newborn blessed and fortunate. At the birth of John, the neighbours: what manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him.
“May the new-born be blessed.” The Lord bless thee, and keep thee: the Lord make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee.
A child brought forth from one of Thy servants. Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord.
A branch grown from the tree of Thy mercy. He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season.

“This new flower of the rose-garden.” Wordsworth thought the child arrives with something the adult loses: the Soul that rises with us, our life’s Star, cometh from afar. The prayers ask that the child be trained and educated. Is childhood, in these prayers, a fullness to be kept or a capacity to be developed?
Make these children excellent plants. Thy children like olive plants round about thy table.
“O God! Educate these children.” And all thy children shall be taught of the Lord; and great shall be the peace of thy children.
Children as branches of the tree of life. Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.

Lovely children, “the handiwork of the fingers of Thy might”. Blake, looking at a fiercer creature: did he who made the Lamb make thee? Children are not only lambs. What do these prayers ask for the child’s strength and will?
Guard the children born in Thy day. Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Thanks that Thou hast preferred these small children. Thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.
Aid Thy servants to establish schools in every region. Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way.
Confirm them in the acquisition of knowledge. From a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise.
“O dear child! I hope that thou mayest become a son of the Kingdom.” Except ye become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
May God assist thee in the days of thy youth. Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not.
A youth who has grown up in obedience. Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers.
Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
“You have granted him daughters”: preserve them. Of Job’s daughters: in all the land were no women found so fair; and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
Assist my son and daughter to remember and praise You. Abraham’s prayer: my Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity also.
Grant to each of Thy servants pure offspring. Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for those who ward off evil.
“Bestow upon me a righteous child.” Zachariah’s prayer in the Qur’an: my Lord! Bestow upon me of Thy bounty goodly offspring. Lo! Thou art the Hearer of Prayer.
Ordain for my son what will make him hold fast. Luqmán to his son: O my dear son! Establish worship and enjoin kindness and forbid iniquity, and persevere whatever may befall thee.
A servant and the son of a servant. The unfeigned faith that dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also.
Assist the children he left behind to follow in his steps. Elisha, of his master: let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.
Bless the members of this household. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
“I am but a little child; make Thine Arm a dear resting-place.” And a little child shall lead them.

shortfall: The prayers of readings 14 to 32 for infants and for groups of children use one family of images (sapling, flower, branch, pearl) many times over, and readings 46 to 53 are petitions for offspring alike in form; the companions given serve each group, and about a third of the guide’s number was left unplaced.

psalm-plants-grown-up-in-their-youth.text: That our sons may be as plants grown up in their youth; that our daughters may be as corner stones, polished after the similitude of a palace

luke-what-manner-of-child.text: And all they that heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him

psalm-hope-upon-my-mothers-breasts.text: But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts. I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly

psalm-wherewithal-shall-a-young-man.text: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word

quran-vowed-that-which-is-in-my-belly.text: (Remember) when the wife of 'Imran said: My Lord! I have vowed unto Thee that which is in my belly as a consecrated (offering). Accept it from me. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Hearer, the Knower!
